about: Radiology Partners is a Nashville-based radiology practice, one of the largest in the US, providing radiologists to hospitals and imaging centres through about 3,000 doctors and an AI-enabled workflow. Customers are hospitals and health systems, with revenue in the billions. It is backed by Nighthawk, Lead Edge, Gates and others and by investors such as Welsh Carson. A B2B medical services brand with low public awareness.

Apotex is a Canadian pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Toronto and founded in 1974 by Barry Sherman, that is Canada's largest generic drug maker. It develops, manufactures and sells generic medicines, biosimilars and some specialty and consumer health products in Canada, the US and other markets, with thousands of employees. It sells to pharmacies, hospitals and health systems and is privately held. Well-known healthcare name in Canada, but a B2B-focused brand.

Clariane is a French operator of nursing homes, post-acute and rehabilitation clinics, mental health clinics and home care, headquartered in Paris and listed on Euronext Paris. Formerly Korian, it was renamed Clariane in 2023. It operates more than 1,000 facilities in France, Germany, Belgium, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and the UK, with around 60,000 employees and revenue of about 5 billion euros. It is paid by residents, insurers and public health systems. Known in its home markets as a care provider, not a consumer marketer.

CMR Surgical is a Cambridge, UK medical robotics company, founded in 2014, that makes the Versius surgical robot, a modular, portable robotic system for minimally invasive keyhole surgery. It sells or leases to hospitals in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, Latin America and the US, and earns revenue from systems, instruments and services. It has raised about $1.7 billion in funding from investors including SoftBank, Tencent and Cambridge Innovation Capital. B2B medical device brand, known to hospitals and surgeons but not consumers.

Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, listed on Nasdaq and NYSE (LIN), formed in 2018 from the merger of Linde AG and Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon and specialty gases, plus engineering and equipment, to healthcare, chemicals, energy, food, electronics and manufacturing customers in over 100 countries. Revenue is about $33 billion and it has around 65,000 employees. The Crunchbase listing shows the Woking, UK base of its engineering operations. B2B giant with low consumer awareness.

SSM Health is a Catholic, not-for-profit health system based in St. Louis, Missouri, operating hospitals, physician practices, urgent care and post-acute care in Missouri, Illinois, Oklahoma and Wisconsin. It employs over 30,000 people and has tens of thousands of physicians and staff, with revenue of about $10 billion, and runs the SSM Health Cardinal Glennon Children's Hospital. Patients and insurers pay for services. Strong regional brand in the Midwest.

Molina Healthcare is a Long Beach, California-based US health insurer, listed on the NYSE (MOH), serving Medicaid, Medicare and marketplace members, with about 5 million members and revenue of around $40 billion. Founded in 1980 by Dr. C. David Molina. Customers are state governments and individuals on subsidised plans. Moderate US brand awareness through advertising.

Oscar Health is a New York-based US health insurer, listed on the NYSE (OSCR), selling individual and family ACA marketplace plans and Medicare Advantage with a technology-led, consumer-friendly approach. Co-founded in 2012 by Mario Schlosser and Josh Kushner. About 2 million members and revenue of over $9 billion. Consumer brand, with substantial advertising in the US.

Owens & Minor is a Glen Allen, Virginia-based healthcare logistics company, listed on the NYSE (OMI), distributing medical and surgical supplies to hospitals and manufacturing medical products (Halyard). It also has home health business Apria. Revenue is about $10 billion. B2B with strong healthcare industry recognition and little consumer branding.

Surgery Partners is a Brentwood, Tennessee-based owner and operator of surgical facilities, listed on Nasdaq (SGRY), with majority ownership by Bain Capital, running ambulatory surgery centres and surgical hospitals in about 30 US states. Revenue is about $3 billion. Healthcare provider brand with local recognition.

CeQur is a Swiss medical device company based in Horw, near Lucerne, that develops wearable drug delivery devices. Its main product is the PaQ insulin delivery device, a simple patch-like insulin pump worn on the body for people with type 2 diabetes who need mealtime insulin. Customers are patients, diabetes clinics and health systems, in the US and Europe, with revenue from device and consumable sales. It is venture-backed and privately held. It has some patient and clinician awareness but is not a mainstream consumer brand, so limited sponsorship potential.
cb_desc: CeQur develops drug delivery devices..

about: BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) is a Franklin Lakes, New Jersey medical technology company, making syringes, needles, catheters, infusion pumps, diagnostics and biosciences products. Founded in 1897, it has about 70,000 employees and revenue of around $20 billion, listed on the NYSE (BDX). It sells to hospitals, labs and pharma companies worldwide. A B2B healthcare brand with low consumer awareness.

Fresenius is a German health care group headquartered in Bad Homburg, with business units Fresenius Kabi (injectable drugs, clinical nutrition, biosimilars), Fresenius Helios (Europe's largest private hospital operator) and a stake in dialysis company Fresenius Medical Care, formerly a subsidiary. Revenue is about 22 billion euros with roughly 190,000 employees. Founded in 1912 and listed on the Frankfurt exchange (FRE). Mainly B2B with a strong Helios brand in Germany and Spain.

Hims & Hers Health is a telehealth company, listed on the NYSE (HIMS) and based in San Francisco, selling consumer health products by online consultation and subscription. Its range covers erectile dysfunction, hair loss, skin care, mental health, weight loss and women's health. Founded in 2017 as Hims, it earns revenue of over $1.5 billion with millions of subscribers. Strong US direct-to-consumer brand awareness, with heavy advertising, including a Super Bowl presence.

about: Rede D'Or Sao Luiz is Brazil's largest private hospital network, based in Rio de Janeiro, with more than 70 hospitals and oncology and diagnostic units, plus the SulAmerica insurance business it acquired. Founded in 1977 by Jorge Moll, it is listed on the B3 (RDOR3). Customers are patients, insurers and corporate clients. Strong brand in Brazilian healthcare, so a possible local health sponsor.

Sutter Health is a non-profit integrated health system in Northern California, based in Sacramento, with about 24 hospitals, outpatient surgery centres, a large medical group and home health services. It treats millions of patients and has revenue of over $15 billion. Customers are patients and insurers. It is a strong regional healthcare brand with a record of local sports and community sponsorship, but of limited national appeal.

Universal Health Services (UHS) is a King of Prussia, Pennsylvania hospital operator listed on the NYSE (UHS), running behavioural health facilities and acute care hospitals in the US and UK. It is one of the largest hospital companies, with revenue of about $15 billion and around 90,000 employees. Customers are patients and insurers. B2B-like healthcare brand with low consumer marketing appeal.

Verano Holdings is a Chicago multi-state cannabis operator, vertically integrated, with cultivation, processing and over 100 Zen Leaf, MKT and other branded dispensaries across the US. It is listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (VRNO) and has revenue of roughly $900 million. Customers are medical and adult-use consumers. Cannabis marketing is legally restricted, so sponsorship fit is poor.

Cityblock Health is a Brooklyn, New York healthcare provider that delivers tech-enabled, community-based primary care and behavioural health to Medicaid and Medicare patients in underserved communities, working with health plans. Founded in 2017 by Toyin Ajayi and others as a Google-linked venture, it has raised several hundred million dollars. B2B2C with limited general brand awareness.

Ensign Group is a US provider of skilled nursing, senior living and rehabilitation services, listed on Nasdaq (ENSG) and operating around 350 facilities in 15 states. It was based in Utah per the input and runs a model of decentralised, locally led facilities. Revenue is about $4 billion. Customers are patients and government payers such as Medicare and Medicaid. Healthcare operator with limited consumer brand awareness.

Fakeeh.Care is the healthcare group built around the Dr. Soliman Fakeeh Hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, a leading private hospital founded in 1978 that offers internal medicine, urology, ENT, emergency and many other specialties. It has expanded with hospitals in Dubai and Riyadh and a university and nursing college. Customers are patients and insurers. A well known private healthcare brand in Saudi Arabia, a F1 host country.
cb_desc: Fakeeh.Care specializes in internal medicine, urology, EN..

about: ModivCare is a Denver healthcare services company, listed on Nasdaq (MODV), providing non-emergency medical transportation, personal care and remote patient monitoring, mostly funded by Medicaid and managed care organisations in the US. Revenue is around $2.8 billion. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2025 after heavy debt. Low consumer brand awareness and weak financial position.

Teleflex is a Wayne, Pennsylvania medical technology company, listed on the NYSE (TFX), making devices for critical care, surgery and interventional procedures, such as catheters, vascular access, and the Arrow and UroLift brands. Revenue is about $3 billion. It sells to hospitals and clinicians, and has no consumer brand recognition.

VillageMD is a Chicago-based primary care provider operating physician-led clinics and value-based care networks across the US, backed by Walgreens, which invested over 5 billion dollars to take a majority stake. It runs Village Medical, Summit Health and CityMD clinics, many of them co-located in Walgreens pharmacies. It grew rapidly but closed many clinics from 2023 as Walgreens retrenched. Recorded funding is about 7 billion dollars. Privately held. Healthcare brand with local patient awareness.

LifePoint Health is a Brentwood, Tennessee hospital operator, with about 60 community hospitals and many outpatient and rehabilitation facilities in the US, mainly in smaller communities. It was acquired by Apollo Global Management funds in 2018 and merged with Kindred Healthcare's hospital business to form ScionHealth in 2021, while LifePoint Health continued as an operating brand. It earns patient service revenue. Privately held. Local hospital brand with community recognition.

Mehilainen is Finland's largest private healthcare provider, based in Helsinki, running clinics, hospitals, diagnostic and occupational health services, elderly care and mental health care in Finland, Estonia and Sweden. It has revenue of more than 1 billion euros and serves public sector customers, insurers, employers and private patients. It is privately held and owned by private equity investors. Recorded funding is about 2 billion euros. Strong healthcare consumer brand in Finland.

Nutex Health is a Houston-based healthcare services company that owns and operates micro-hospitals and freestanding emergency rooms in Texas and several other states, together with a population health management arm and an independent physician association network. Revenue comes from patient services and value-based care contracts, and is around 500 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (NUTX). Recorded funding is about 2.4 billion dollars. Regional healthcare brand with local patient awareness.

Ramsay Sante is a French private hospital and primary care group, headquartered in Paris, formed from the former Generale de Sante. It operates about 350 hospitals and clinics in France, Italy, Sweden, Denmark and Norway, and is majority owned by Australia's Ramsay Health Care, with Predica (Credit Agricole Assurances) as a significant shareholder. Revenue is above 5 billion euros. Large healthcare brand in Europe, with regional patient awareness.

Advanz Pharma is a specialty pharmaceutical company with its headquarters in London, focused on hospital medicines and rare disease, with a portfolio of off-patent and biosimilar products sold in Europe, plus Mississauga operations in Canada. It was taken private by Nordic Capital in 2021 after a Canadian listing. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems. Revenue is above 1 billion euros. B2B healthcare brand with no consumer awareness.

Aledade is a Bethesda, Maryland healthcare company that helps independent primary care practices join accountable care organisations and succeed in value-based care, giving them technology, analytics and operational support. It works with thousands of physicians across about 40 US states, earning shared savings and management fees from Medicare and other payers. It was founded in 2014 by Farzad Mostashari and has raised about 1.2 billion dollars. Privately held. B2B healthcare brand known in the medical community.

Ardent Health Services is a Nashville-based hospital operator, running about 30 acute care hospitals and hundreds of outpatient sites across several US states, including Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Idaho, Kansas and New Jersey, with its employed physician groups. Revenue is more than 6 billion dollars. It listed on the NYSE (ARDT) in 2024, with Equity Group Investments as the largest holder. Customers are patients and health plans. Regional healthcare brand with local visibility.

US healthcare services company that helps physician groups and health plans run value-based care, with offerings including Evolent Care Partners for specialty and complex care management and technology-enabled specialty benefit management in oncology, cardiology and musculoskeletal care. Customers are health insurers, Medicaid plans and provider organisations, who pay fees and a share of savings. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, with several thousand staff and annual revenue of roughly $2.5 billion. Listed on the NYSE (EVH) since its 2015 IPO. B2B healthcare brand with low consumer visibility.

Late-stage US biotech founded by billionaire Patrick Soon-Shiong, developing immunotherapies for cancer and infectious disease. Its lead product Anktiva (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept) won FDA approval in 2024 for BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. Revenue comes from drug sales and licensing, with customers being hospitals and oncology clinics and funding largely from Soon-Shiong. Based in San Diego area California; listed on Nasdaq (IBRX) after a 2021 merger with NantKwest. Low consumer brand awareness; known to investors and clinicians.

US medical device company that makes the Tablo hemodialysis system, a portable all-in-one machine aimed at taking dialysis from clinics to acute care hospitals and, potentially, the home. Sells consoles and consumable cartridges to hospitals, dialysis providers and, increasingly, home patients. Based in San Jose, California, and listed on Nasdaq (OM) since its 2020 IPO. Has faced FDA clearance setbacks and raised large venture and public funds. B2B healthcare brand with minimal consumer visibility.

Major US healthcare distribution and manufacturing company based in Dublin, Ohio, that distributes pharmaceuticals, medical and laboratory products to pharmacies and hospitals, and makes medical products under the Cardinal Health brand. Revenue exceeds $200 billion a year, with around 48,000 employees and a place near the top of the Fortune 500. Listed on the NYSE (CAH). Also runs nuclear pharmacy and at-home care services. Large B2B brand; known to healthcare buyers but little retail consumer visibility.

Melbourne, Australia, health business, described as providing affordable access to health and wellness products. Crunchbase classes it under health care and personal health, with total funding of A$1.6 billion shown for August 2025, which is very large for the sector and likely reflects an acquisition or debt financing. Customers are presumably consumers and retail partners. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: US value-based kidney care company that manages care for patients with advanced kidney disease and operates in partnership with health plans, nephrologists and Medicare Advantage programmes. Earns revenue as a share of reduced medical costs for the populations it manages. Based in Denver, Colorado, venture-backed, with total funding of about $936 million and a round shown in September 2025. B2B health care provider with minimal consumer brand awareness.

Mater Private Hospital is a private Catholic hospital in Dublin, Ireland, part of the Mater Private Network, offering cardiac care, cancer treatment, emergency medicine, orthopaedics and diagnostics to patients covered by private health insurance or self-paying. Crunchbase shows about 820 million in funding in September 2026. Customers are Irish private patients and insurers, and it is one of the larger private hospitals in the country. Local healthcare brand in Ireland, with moderate recognition among Irish consumers and none elsewhere.
cb_desc: Mater Private Hospital is a private Catholic hospital offer...

about: Medicover is an international healthcare and diagnostics group headquartered in Stockholm, founded in 1995, that runs clinics, hospitals, dentistry, laboratory diagnostics and prepaid health plans mainly in Poland, Germany, Romania, Ukraine and India. Customers include corporate employers who buy healthcare packages, private patients and public payers, with revenue above EUR 2 billion and over 40,000 staff. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (MCOV B). Strong brand in Poland and Central Europe, almost none elsewhere.

Aedifica is a Belgian real estate investment trust based in Brussels that owns care homes, senior housing and healthcare properties across Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Finland, Sweden, Ireland and Spain, leasing them to care operators on long leases. Portfolio value is about EUR 6 billion. It is listed on Euronext Brussels (AED), with a secondary listing in Amsterdam. B2B property investor with no consumer brand profile.

Aster DM Healthcare is a healthcare group founded by Dr Azad Moopen in 1987, headquartered in Dubai. It operates hospitals, clinics and retail pharmacies across the GCC under Aster, Medcare and Access brands, and in India through Aster hospitals, serving patients and insurers. Its structure was split between a Gulf business and an Indian business, listed on the NSE and BSE as Aster DM Healthcare. Revenue is over $1 billion. Familiar healthcare brand in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Kerala, with limited global profile.

LifeStance Health is the largest US outpatient mental health provider, based in Scottsdale, Arizona, employing thousands of psychiatrists, psychologists, therapists and nurse practitioners at roughly 600 centres in over 30 states, delivering in-person and telehealth care. Revenue comes from insurers and patients, and is above $1.2 billion a year. Founded in 2017, it is backed by Summit Partners and TPG and listed on Nasdaq (LFST). Local clinic brand with moderate national consumer awareness.

Option Care Health is the largest independent home and alternate-site infusion services provider in the United States, formed in 2019 through the merger of BioScrip and Option Care. It delivers infused and injected medicines and nutrition therapy to patients at home or in infusion suites, with revenue near $5 billion, covering all states. Customers are patients, physicians, hospitals and insurers. Listed on Nasdaq (OPCH). Healthcare services brand with low consumer awareness.

VeraDermics is a US dermatology company based in New Haven, Connecticut, developing prescription treatments for hair loss, with a lead candidate for pattern hair loss, a new extended-release oral therapy. It has no marketed products and is funded by venture and public equity, with about $733 million shown by April 2026. Customers will be dermatologists and patients. Little consumer awareness yet, though hair loss is a large consumer market.

about: Almoosa Specialist Hospital is a private hospital and healthcare group based in Hofuf, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, offering specialist surgical, maternity, cardiac and oncology care to patients in Al Ahsa and nearby cities, with several hospitals and clinics. It was founded in 2008 and is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) after its 2025 IPO. Crunchbase shows SAR 2.49 billion in funding in July 2026. Strong regional brand in the Eastern Province, but no national or international consumer profile.
cb_desc: Almoosa Specialist Hospital is a private hospital and health...

about: Encompass Health is a US post-acute care provider based in Birmingham, Alabama, formerly HealthSouth. It operates about 160 inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in 40 states and Puerto Rico, treating stroke, brain injury, hip fracture and other patients, with revenue of around $5 billion and Medicare as the largest payer. It spun off its home health and hospice business as Enhabit in 2022. Listed on the NYSE (EHC). Well-known local hospital brand, though not a national consumer name.

HistoSonics is a US medical device company based in Plymouth, Minnesota, that makes the Edison system, a non-invasive focused ultrasound platform for histotripsy, which mechanically destroys liver tumours, with FDA clearance in 2023. Customers are hospitals and cancer centres. In 2025 a group of investors including Jeff Bezos acquired a majority stake at about a $2.25 billion valuation. It is private. Visible in medtech and healthcare press but no consumer brand profile.

IKS Health is an Indian healthcare services and technology company that provides physician enablement, clinical documentation, revenue cycle and care coordination services to US healthcare providers, using AI-assisted and human-supported workflows. It is headquartered in Mumbai, with US offices including Dallas, and is listed on the NSE and BSE after a 2024 IPO. Customers are US physician groups and health systems. B2B services firm with no consumer profile.

about: Imperative Care is a US medical technology company based in Campbell, California, developing devices to treat stroke and other vascular conditions, including the Zoom stroke system aspiration catheters and Symphony thrombectomy, plus the Gateway and Zoom product lines. Customers are hospitals and neurovascular specialists. It is venture funded and private, with Crunchbase showing about $659 million raised by March 2026. B2B medtech brand with no consumer awareness.

Privia Health is a US physician enablement company based in Arlington, Virginia, that partners with medical groups and operates accountable care organisations in states such as Maryland, Virginia, Georgia and Texas. It provides technology, back-office services and value-based care support to thousands of physicians, with revenue near $2 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (PRVA) after a 2021 IPO. B2B healthcare services firm with no consumer awareness.

Rayner Surgical Group is a UK ophthalmic medical device maker, based in Worthing, West Sussex, that manufactures intraocular lenses used in cataract surgery, along with related surgical products and implants. Rayner dates back to 1910 and sells to eye surgeons and hospitals in more than 80 countries. Crunchbase shows GBP 500 million in funding in February 2026. B2B medtech with no consumer brand profile.
cb_desc: Rayner Surgical Group is manufactures Intraocular...

about: RiverSpring Living is a US not-for-profit senior care organisation based in the Bronx, New York, formerly the Hebrew Home at Riverdale, providing skilled nursing, assisted living, home care and managed long-term care for older adults. Its health plan arm serves Medicaid-eligible seniors in the New York area. Funding shown is $633 million in February 2026. Regional brand in the New York metro area with little national profile.
cb_desc: RiverSpring Living isapdori nationally recognized leader i..

about: Select Medical is a US healthcare provider based in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania, operating critical illness recovery hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation hospitals, outpatient physical therapy clinics under Select Physical Therapy and the Concentra occupational health centres, which it partly spun off in an IPO in 2024. Revenue is around $5-6 billion. Customers are patients, employers and insurers. Listed on the NYSE (SEM). Local clinic brands, moderate national awareness.

Nomad Health is a New York online staffing marketplace linking nurses, allied health workers and physicians with hospitals and clinics for travel, locum and permanent roles. Founded in 2015, it uses a digital platform for job matching and credentialing. Customers are US healthcare employers and clinicians. It has raised around $274M including venture rounds backed by investors such as General Catalyst. Healthcare staffing brand with moderate recognition among clinicians, and some online and event marketing.
cb_desc: Nomad Health is an online staffing marketplace that...

about: Agilon health is a physician enablement company, listed on the NYSE (AGL), based in Westerville, Ohio. It partners with independent primary care groups and provides technology, data and capital so they can take on risk-based Medicare Advantage contracts, serving seniors across the US. Founded in 2016, it listed in 2021 and has cut growth forecasts and its stock fell sharply after 2024 cost problems. Customers are physician groups and health plans, and the model is not consumer-facing. Low public brand awareness.

Doctolib is a French healthtech company, founded in Paris in 2013, that runs an online and mobile platform for booking medical appointments with doctors and other health professionals, and sells practice management software and teleconsultation tools. It serves tens of millions of patients and hundreds of thousands of practitioners in France, Germany and Italy. It became a unicorn in 2019 and has raised about $1.2B. Strong consumer-facing health brand in France and Germany, with substantial advertising.

MiRus is a Marietta, Georgia medical device company that designs transcatheter heart valve systems and other structural heart products for the treatment of valve disease, including the Siegel TAVR system. It sells to cardiac centres and has raised substantial venture and growth funding, with about $1.57B shown by 2026. The company is smaller than competitors such as Edwards Lifesciences. B2B healthcare brand known to cardiologists, with no consumer awareness. Details should be confirmed.

about: Prime Healthcare Services is one of the largest US hospital systems, based in Ontario, California, owning and operating about 50 acute-care hospitals in 14 states, plus clinics and medical groups. Dr Prem Reddy founded it in 2001 and it remains privately held, with a nonprofit affiliate, Prime Healthcare Foundation, owning Ascension hospitals bought in 2023. It employs tens of thousands of people. Funding of about $1.5B was recorded in 2024. Local hospital brands, with Prime visible in regional sports sponsorships.

Organon is a Jersey City, New Jersey women's health company, spun off from Merck in 2021 and listed on the NYSE (OGN). It sells contraceptives such as Nexplanon, fertility products, biosimilars and a large portfolio of established brands including Singulair and Cozaar, in more than 140 countries, with annual revenue near US$6 billion. Customers are doctors, hospitals and pharmacies. Funding of about $1B was recorded in 2024. Pharma brand with moderate public awareness and a focus on women's health.

Alvogen is a Morristown, New Jersey pharmaceutical company, founded by Robert Wessman, that develops and sells generic and specialty medicines and biosimilars in the US, Europe and emerging markets. It built its business through acquisitions, and its US business was sold in 2021 to Lotus Pharmaceutical-led buyers, while the rest of the group operates internationally. Funding of about $769M was recorded in 2025. B2B pharma brand known to pharmacists and distributors, with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Alvogen develops, mark manufactures, and markets...

about: Bioventus is a Durham, North Carolina medical device and orthobiologics company, listed on Nasdaq (BVS), that sells products for bone healing and joint pain, including Exogen ultrasound bone healing systems, Durolane and Euflexxa hyaluronic acid injections, and surgical products. It sells through orthopaedic doctors and hospitals, with growth through acquisitions such as Misonix. Customers are physicians and patients. Funding of about $827M was recorded in 2025, mostly debt. Healthcare brand with recognition among orthopaedists, but low general public awareness.

Envision Healthcare was a Nashville, Tennessee physician staffing and outpatient care company that provided emergency, anaesthesia and radiology services to hospitals, plus ambulatory surgery centres and AMR ambulances. KKR took it private in 2018 for about US$9.9 billion, and it filed for Chapter 11 in 2023, then emerged as a smaller group after lenders took control and sold units. Funding of about $750M is recorded in 2025. B2B healthcare services brand, with low consumer awareness beyond AMR.

Judi Health, formerly Capital Rx, is a New York health technology company that provides pharmacy benefit management and health plan administration for employers, unions and health plans, using transparent pass-through pricing and its Judi platform. Founded in 2016 by AJ Loiacono, it rebranded to Judi Health in 2025 and has raised about $736M. Customers are self-insured employers and plan sponsors. B2B healthcare technology brand known in benefits circles, with limited consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Judi Health is a healthtech platform that provides...

about: Stevanato Group is an Italian maker of glass vials, syringes, cartridges and drug delivery devices, plus analytical and testing services for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, based in Piombino Dese near Padua. Founded in 1949 by the Stevanato family, it is listed on the NYSE (STVN) and has annual revenue of about EUR 1.1 billion with plants in Europe, the US, China and Mexico. Funding of about $798M was recorded in 2025. B2B supplier to drug makers with no consumer awareness.

Apollo Hospitals Enterprise is India's largest private healthcare group, based in Chennai and founded in 1983 by Dr Prathap C. Reddy, operating about 10,000 beds in more than 70 hospitals, plus Apollo Pharmacy (the largest chain in India), Apollo 24/7 digital health and diagnostics clinics. It is listed on the NSE and BSE (APOLLOHOSP). Customers are patients across India and international medical tourists. Funding of about $665M was recorded in 2025. Very strong consumer healthcare brand in India, with a record of sports and cause marketing.

Chartwell Retirement Residences is Canada's largest operator of seniors housing, based in Mississauga, Ontario, and listed on the TSX (CSH.UN). It owns and manages more than 200 retirement residences and long-term care homes in Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia and Alberta, serving more than 25,000 residents with services that range from independent living to assisted care. Funding of about C$800M was recorded in 2025, including debt. Familiar local brand to older adults and their families, with limited sports sponsorship.

Solventum is a health care company spun off from 3M in April 2024, based near Minneapolis, Minnesota (Maplewood) and listed on the NYSE (SOLV). It sells medical and surgical products, wound care, dental solutions, purification and filtration, and health information software, with annual revenue near US$8 billion, to hospitals, clinicians and dentists worldwide. Funding of about $648M was recorded in 2025. Customers are health providers. The brand is new, but products such as Tegaderm and Filtrete heritage are familiar to professionals.

Therme Group is a Vienna-based wellness and leisure company that develops and operates large thermal spa and entertainment resorts, including Therme Bucharest in Romania, Therme Erding in Germany (as a technology partner), and planned venues in Manchester, Poland and elsewhere. Customers are families and leisure visitors, who pay entry fees. Funding of about EUR 565M was recorded in 2025. Founded by Robert Hanea, it has a strong wellness and sustainability story, and some brand awareness in central Europe and the UK.
cb_desc: Therme Group is a global technology company.

about: Vitalia Home is a Spanish care home group, based in Zaragoza, Aragon, running residences for older adults across Spain, with services that range from independent living to nursing care. It has grown through acquisitions of residences. Funding of about EUR 500M was recorded in 2025, mostly investor and debt financing. Customers are elderly residents and families. Regional care brand in Spain, with limited national consumer awareness. Details on the number of residences and ownership should be confirmed.
cb_desc: Vitalia Home is a Spanish care home group.

about: Rythm Health is a San Francisco company that Crunchbase says designs and develops consumer lab testing products, classed under health care and wellness. It likely sells at-home or direct-to-consumer health tests, but product names, customers and scale are not stated. Crunchbase shows total funding of about $157 million, with the latest round in June 2026. Ownership is not detailed in the supplied data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Rythm designs and develops consumer lab testing product...

about: Burjeel Holdings is the largest private healthcare group in Abu Dhabi, founded by Dr Shamsheer Vayalil and part of VPS Healthcare. It operates hospitals, day-surgery centres, clinics and pharmacies in the UAE and Oman under Burjeel, Medeor, Lifecare and other brands, and earns money from patient and insurance payments. It listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (BURJEEL) in October 2022, with annual revenue near AED 5 billion. Strong regional consumer healthcare brand in the Gulf, with a high-income customer base.

Distalmotion is a Swiss medical device company, based in Epalinges near Lausanne, that makes the Dexter robotic surgical system, a more modular and compact robot for minimally invasive surgery in urology, gynaecology and general surgery. It sells systems and single-use instruments to hospitals and ambulatory surgery centres in Europe and the US. It is private and venture-backed, having raised over $450 million including a major recent round. It competes with Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci. B2B medical technology brand with low consumer awareness.

Omada Health is a San Francisco digital health company that offers virtual chronic-condition care programmes for diabetes prevention, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, musculoskeletal pain and weight management, including GLP-1 support. Members get coaching, connected devices (scales, glucose meters) and app-based support, paid for by employers, health plans and government programmes. Founded in 2011, it listed on Nasdaq (OMDA) in June 2025. Crunchbase shows about $540 million raised pre-IPO. B2B2C health brand reaching hundreds of thousands of members, with moderate public awareness.

United Imaging Healthcare is a Shanghai-based medical imaging and radiotherapy equipment maker producing MRI, CT, PET/CT, X-ray and ultrasound systems and radiotherapy equipment, sold to hospitals in China and increasingly overseas. Customers are hospitals and clinics, and revenue comes from equipment sales and service. It is a leading domestic competitor to GE, Siemens and Philips, and listed on the Shanghai STAR Market (688271) in 2022. Founded in 2011. B2B medical technology brand, mainly known within healthcare; limited consumer awareness.

InflaRx is a German biotech based in Jena, developing complement-inhibiting antibody drugs for inflammatory diseases. Its anti-C5a antibody vilobelimab received emergency use authorisation in the US for severe Covid-19 and is being studied in skin diseases such as pyoderma gangrenosum, while an oral C5aR inhibitor is also in development. It has been listed on Nasdaq (IFRX) since 2017. Customers are hospitals and pharma partners. Revenue is small and it relies on equity raising, with about $437 million raised. B2B biotech with no consumer awareness.

Kestra Medical Technologies is a Kirkland, Washington medical device company that makes the ASSURE wearable cardioverter defibrillator, a vest-like device that monitors heart rhythm and delivers a shock to patients at risk of sudden cardiac arrest, plus a remote-monitoring service. Customers are patients prescribed the device by cardiologists, with revenue from insurers. Listed on Nasdaq (KMTS) following an IPO in 2025. Competes with Zoll LifeVest. Crunchbase shows about $409 million raised. Healthcare B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Musely is a Santa Clara, California based prescription wellness and telehealth company offering custom-compounded dermatology products for hyperpigmentation, acne and ageing, and prescription weight-loss and women's health treatments, sold direct to consumers online with remote doctor consultations. Customers are mostly women buying skincare and wellness online, and revenue comes from product subscriptions. It is privately held, with about $388 million shown in funding in May 2026. Direct-to-consumer health brand marketed heavily online.

about: Nyxoah is a Belgian medical device company based in Mont-Saint-Guibert that makes the Genio system, a neurostimulation implant for obstructive sleep apnea that treats the condition by stimulating the hypoglossal nerve. It sells in Europe and received US FDA approval in 2025. Customers are sleep physicians, surgeons and patients, and revenue is growing but small. Listed on Nasdaq (NYXH), IPO in 2021. Competes with Inspire Medical. B2B medtech with limited consumer awareness.

Rightway is a New York health technology company that provides pharmacy benefit management (PBM) and navigation tools to employers and health plans, with a focus on transparency, a member app, and clinical support for prescriptions and care. Customers are self-insured employers and health plans, and revenue comes from administrative fees and rebates. Founded in 2016, it has raised about $394 million from investors such as Founders Fund and Tiger Global. Private B2B2C brand with limited awareness among employees of client firms.

Talkiatry is a New York-based virtual psychiatry practice offering mental health care through video visits with board-certified psychiatrists, covered by health insurance, for conditions such as depression, anxiety, ADHD and bipolar disorder. Patients book online, and revenue comes from insurance reimbursements. Founded in 2020, it operates across a large number of US states and has raised about $450 million from investors including General Catalyst and Tiger Global. Direct-to-consumer digital health brand with growing awareness through online and advertising campaigns.

Thyme Care is a Nashville-based healthcare company providing value-based cancer care management for health plans, using nurses, navigators and technology to support patients and oncologists and cut avoidable emergency visits. Customers are insurers and cancer practices, and it earns revenue from care-management fees and shared savings. Founded in 2020 by former Flatiron Health executives, it has raised about $400 million from investors such as General Catalyst and Lead Edge. B2B healthcare brand with little consumer awareness.

WELL Health Technologies is a Vancouver-based Canadian digital health company that owns and operates primary care clinics, a virtual care business, electronic medical record software (including OSCAR), and a growing digital healthcare services arm with US and international acquisitions. Customers are patients, physicians and health systems; revenue is over C$1 billion. Listed on the TSX (WELL), founded in 2010. Regional healthcare brand with moderate consumer visibility in Canada, and the owner of well-known clinic networks.

Auna is a Latin American healthcare company based in Lima, Peru, operating private hospitals and clinics, oncology centres, health insurance plans and health-management services in Peru, Mexico and Colombia. It earns money from patient care, premiums and related services, and serves millions of insured members. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange as AUNA in late 2024 and also has funding from private equity. It has a recognised brand in Peru, with a hospital-based rather than mass consumer profile.

Aveanna Healthcare is an Atlanta-based provider of home health services focusing on children and adults, including private duty nursing, therapy, pediatric hospice and medical day centres, with hundreds of locations in over 30 US states. Revenue, in the billions of dollars, comes mainly from Medicaid and other government programmes and insurers. It listed on Nasdaq as AVAH in 2021 after private-equity ownership by Bain Capital. A B2B-ish healthcare provider, known to patients and families locally but not a mainstream consumer brand.

Garofalo Health Care is an Italian private healthcare group, based in Rome, that owns and runs hospitals, outpatient clinics, diagnostic centres, rehabilitation and long-term care facilities, mostly in northern and central Italy, under local brands, working with public health service and private insurers. It was founded by the Garofalo family and listed on Borsa Italiana (Euronext Milan) as GHC in 2018. Crunchbase shows about 275 million euros of financing. A regional healthcare group with local brands and little national consumer branding.

Flo Health is a London-based digital health company, founded in 2015 by Dmitry and Yury Gurski, that operates the Flo app for period tracking, fertility, pregnancy and women's health, using artificial intelligence to provide cycle predictions and health insights. It has hundreds of millions of downloads and tens of millions of monthly active users globally, and earns from premium subscriptions. General Atlantic led a 200 million dollar investment in 2024, valuing it at about 1 billion dollars. A high-profile consumer health brand, particularly with young women.

IVC Evidensia is one of the world's largest veterinary groups, formed in 2019 by the merger of IVC (UK) and Evidensia (Sweden). It runs over 3,000 veterinary clinics and hospitals in about 20 European and North American countries, with revenue from vet services, diagnostics and pet care. Based in Bristol, UK, it is owned by private equity firm EQT with other investors. Raised billions in debt and equity. Pet-owner facing local clinic brands; the group name is B2B.

Boiron is a French pharmaceutical company, based near Lyon, and the world's largest maker of homeopathic medicines, with brands such as Oscillococcinum, Arnica and Camilia. It sells through pharmacies and retail in about 50 countries, with revenue near 500 million euros and several thousand employees. Founded in 1932 and listed on Euronext Paris (BOI). Consumer health brand with wide pharmacy visibility, though homeopathy is controversial in some markets.

Merit Medical Systems is a Utah-based maker of single-use medical devices for interventional and diagnostic procedures, including catheters, guidewires, embolotherapy products, drainage and biopsy tools. Listed on Nasdaq (MMSI), with revenue about 1.3 billion dollars and over 7,000 employees. Customers are hospitals and physicians in about 140 countries. Funding around 1.07 billion dollars reflects debt financing. B2B medical device brand with no consumer recognition.

NantHealth is a healthcare IT company founded by Patrick Soon-Shiong, which offered the Eviti oncology decision support platform plus connected care and payer platforms. It listed on Nasdaq (NH) in 2016 and was delisted around 2023 after financial trouble, with its assets later sold. Customers were health plans, providers and cancer centres. Funding records show about 980 million dollars. B2B with limited public awareness.

about: U Mobile is a Malaysian mobile network operator based in Kuala Lumpur, offering prepaid and postpaid mobile, broadband and digital services to consumers and businesses. Founded in 2007, it is known for its low-cost plans and for being chosen as the operator of Malaysia's second 5G network in 2024. Funding of 4.3 billion Malaysian ringgit in 2024 supports the 5G build-out. Visible consumer telecom brand in Malaysia.
cb_desc: UMobile is an application developing company.

about: EuroAPI is a Paris-based maker of active pharmaceutical ingredients, spun out of Sanofi in 2022 and listed on Euronext Paris (EAPI). It produces APIs for third-party drug makers and for Sanofi at six sites in France, Germany, Hungary, Italy and the UK, serving oncology, anti-infective and other therapies. Revenue is about 1 billion euros and it has about 3,000 employees. B2B pharmaceutical supplier with no consumer brand.

Molnlycke Health Care is a Swedish medical products group from Gothenburg, one of the world's largest makers of advanced wound care (Mepilex, Mepitel) and operating room products and surgical solutions. Customers are hospitals and healthcare providers in about 100 countries, with revenue near 2 billion euros and around 8,000 employees. Controlled by the Swedish investment group Investor AB. Funding of about 792 million dollars recorded in 2025. B2B medical brand with little consumer recognition.

about: PROCEPT BioRobotics is a San Jose, California medical device company that makes the AquaBeam robotic system for Aquablation therapy, a waterjet treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia. Listed on Nasdaq (PRCT) since 2021, with revenue growing quickly to over 200 million dollars. Customers are urologists and hospitals, mainly in the US. Funding around 820 million dollars including public offerings. B2B medical technology, with patient-directed marketing but no wide consumer profile.

Siloam Hospitals is an Indonesian hospital operator based in Tangerang, Banten, part of the Lippo Group, running the country's largest private hospital network of about 40 hospitals across Indonesia, along with clinics and medical education. Listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (SILO). Customers are patients, insurers and corporates. Founded in 1996. Revenue is over 10 trillion rupiah. Recognisable healthcare consumer brand in Indonesia.

Lundbeck is a Danish pharmaceutical company in Copenhagen specialising in brain diseases, including depression (Trintellix), schizophrenia (Abilify Maintena, Rexulti), Parkinson's, migraine (Vyepti) and epilepsy. Founded in 1915 and majority-controlled by the Lundbeck Foundation, it is listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (LUN B) with revenue near 2.5 billion euros and about 5,000 employees. Sells through physicians and hospitals worldwide. Strong sector name; limited consumer recognition.

Cerebral is a US digital mental health company providing online psychiatry, therapy and medication management through a subscription telehealth app, treating anxiety, depression, ADHD and other conditions. Founded in 2019 and registered in Delaware, it expanded fast during the pandemic, then faced federal investigation over ADHD prescribing practices and a leadership change in 2022 and 2023. Funding of about 487 million dollars. Heavily advertised consumer brand through social and TV ads, but with reputational risk.

Dedalus Group is a healthcare software company based in Florence, Italy, providing hospital information systems, clinical, radiology, laboratory and diagnostic software to hospitals and healthcare networks in over 40 countries. It is owned by private equity group Ardian and has grown by acquiring DXC's healthcare unit and Agfa HealthCare's IT business. About 7,000 employees and annual revenue of around 1 billion euros. B2B vendor with low public awareness.

GI Alliance is the largest US gastroenterology physician group, based in Southlake, Texas, with over 700 gastroenterologists and several hundred clinics and endoscopy centres. It is backed by private equity firm Apollo, which took a majority stake in 2021, and has since added further investors. Funding around 515 million dollars. Patients are consumers, but the group brand is low-profile. B2B-style healthcare services platform with regional clinic names.

Main Street Health is a Nashville-based primary care provider operating value-based clinics for older adults on Medicare Advantage, with around 100 clinics across the US South and Midwest. Backed by private equity, with funding of about 499 million dollars. Revenue is mainly fees paid by Medicare Advantage health plans. Patients are seniors; the brand is local and has low public awareness, with limited consumer marketing.

about: NeuroPace is a Mountain View, California medical device company that makes the RNS System, an implanted device that detects and responds to epileptic seizure activity in the brain, to treat drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Listed on Nasdaq (NPCE) since 2021, with revenue near 80 million dollars. Customers are neurologists and epilepsy centres. Funding of about 457 million dollars. B2B medical technology, with patient-directed outreach but no broad consumer brand.

Saluda Medical is a medical device company making the Evoke closed-loop spinal cord stimulation system for chronic pain, which measures nerve responses and adjusts therapy automatically. It originated in Australia and is based in Bloomington, Minnesota for US operations, with about 530 million dollars raised. Customers are pain specialists and hospitals, with revenue from device sales. B2B medical technology with limited consumer recognition.

about: MJH Life Sciences is a New Jersey-based healthcare media and events business that publishes medical journals and websites such as OncLive, Pharmacy Times, Managed Healthcare Executive and Dermatology Times, and organises healthcare conferences. Revenue comes from pharmaceutical advertising and events. Backed by private equity with 430 million dollars of funding recorded. B2B professional media with no consumer-facing profile or public brand awareness.

Predictive Oncology is a Pittsburgh-based healthcare AI company that uses machine learning on tumour data and 3D tumour models to help drug developers predict how cancers respond to treatments, through its Helomics and Skyline divisions. Listed on Nasdaq (POAI), with very small revenues. The 438 million dollar funding figure in the record looks overstated. B2B research services with no consumer brand.

about: Thrive Pet Healthcare is an Austin-based US veterinary hospital network offering wellness, emergency and specialty care, with more than 380 locations across about 40 states, mostly under local clinic names. Private equity backed, founded in 2019, with 386 million dollars of funding recorded. Customers are pet owners. Group brand has low public awareness, so visibility comes through local clinics rather than a national consumer brand.

about: Treace Medical Concepts is a Ponte Vedra, Florida medical device company known for the Lapiplasty 3D bunion correction system and related foot and ankle surgery products. Listed on Nasdaq (TMCI) since 2021, with revenue near 200 million dollars. Customers are orthopaedic and podiatric surgeons and hospitals; patients can see direct to consumer marketing. Funding of about 388 million dollars. Niche medtech brand.

Visby Medical is a San Jose diagnostics company that makes a handheld, single-use, PCR-based point-of-care test for sexually transmitted infections, and received FDA clearance in 2023 for its Women's Sexual Health Test. It also pushed into at-home testing and respiratory products. Customers are clinics, pharmacies and consumers. Funding of about 436 million dollars. Emerging healthcare brand with moderate public profile.

Accendra Health is the name taken by the home-based healthcare business of Owens and Minor after that group sold its products and healthcare services unit. It provides home respiratory, sleep apnoea and diabetes supplies through Apria, and patient supply services through Byram Healthcare, from a base in Glen Allen, Virginia. Customers are patients at home, referred by physicians and paid by insurers and Medicare. Funding of $326 million is shown for 2026. Healthcare brand with some consumer recognition, mainly among patients.

about: Aidacare is an Australian provider of medical equipment and home care products, based in Sydney, supplying mobility aids, hospital beds, pressure care cushions, respiratory and daily living products to individuals, hospitals, aged care homes and government schemes such as the NDIS. It sells through retail stores, online, and service contracts. It is privately held with investor backing. Funding of about 540 million Australian dollars is shown for 2026. Known to Australian carers and patients, though not a mass-market consumer brand.

about: Cleveland Clinic is a US non-profit academic medical centre based in Cleveland, Ohio, founded in 1921. It runs a main campus and regional hospitals in Ohio and Florida, with international sites in Abu Dhabi, London and Toronto, offering specialist care in cardiac, neurological, digestive and other fields, with about 80,000 caregivers and revenue of around 15 billion dollars. It is a major sports partner of Cleveland teams. Highly recognised healthcare brand in the US.

Grow Therapy is a US mental health platform based in New York, founded in 2020, that connects people with therapists and psychiatric providers who accept their health insurance, including video sessions. It offers practice tools to therapists for billing, scheduling and credentialing. Patients are consumers across most US states, and it has raised more than 300 million dollars, including 2026 funding. It has meaningful consumer advertising, with strong awareness in the mental health space.

KIMS Hospitals (Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences) is an Indian private hospital group based in Secunderabad, Telangana, listed on the NSE and BSE. It runs multi-specialty and tertiary hospitals in Hyderabad, and has expanded to Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Kerala, with several thousand beds. Customers are patients paying directly or through insurance. Revenue is around 30 to 40 billion rupees. Well known hospital brand regionally, mostly in the Telugu states.

about: MMI (Medical Microinstruments) is a medical robotics company founded in Italy and now with a US base in Jacksonville, Florida. Its Symani Surgical System is a robotic platform that helps surgeons perform microsurgery on tiny vessels and nerves, with CE marking and US FDA authorisation in 2024. Customers are hospitals and plastic and reconstructive surgery teams. It is venture backed with about 354 million dollars raised. Specialist device brand with no consumer awareness.

about: Valgen Medtech is a Chinese medical device company based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, focused on structural heart disease, including transcatheter heart valve replacement and repair systems for aortic and tricuspid valve disease. It sells to hospitals and cardiac surgery departments and is backed by investors, with about 376 million dollars raised in 2026. Customers are hospitals and doctors. Specialist device maker with no consumer brand profile.

about: Yatharth Super Speciality Hospitals is an Indian private hospital chain based in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, listed on the NSE and BSE, with hospitals in Noida, Greater Noida, Delhi, Faridabad and nearby cities, offering emergency medicine and multi-specialty care. It has grown by building and acquiring hospitals and has several thousand beds in planning. Customers are patients paying directly or through insurance. Funding of about 32.7 billion rupees is shown for 2026. Regionally known hospital brand.

about: Cala Health is a US bioelectronic medicine company based in San Mateo, California, whose Cala Trio is a wrist-worn device that uses electrical stimulation to reduce hand tremor in people with essential tremor, available by prescription. It also targets conditions such as Parkinson's tremor and overactive bladder. It is venture backed, with about 298 million dollars raised. Customers are neurologists and patients. Niche medical device brand with limited public awareness.

about: Garner Health is a US healthcare navigation company based in New York that uses claims data to steer employees to high-quality, cost-effective doctors and gives them financial rewards for choosing recommended physicians. Employers and health plans pay for the service, aiming to reduce healthcare costs. It was founded in 2020 and has raised about 320 million dollars. B2B health technology brand, with low awareness outside employer benefits circles.

about: Gerresheimer Glas is the glass division of Gerresheimer AG, a German pharmaceutical and healthcare packaging group based in Dusseldorf and listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. It makes glass vials, ampoules, syringes, cartridges, inhalers, insulin pens and cosmetic glass for pharma and biotech customers around the world, with about 10,000 employees and annual revenue of roughly 2 billion euros. Customers are drug makers. B2B supplier with no consumer brand visibility.
